title: General management: housing and incubation
competency: Describe poultry housing needs and natural and artificial incubation.

keywords.def: Keeping fertile eggs warm until they hatch.
A hen sits on the eggs and keeps them warm.
A machine (incubator) keeps eggs warm at a constant temperature.

en.text: Some village households keep chickens inside the house at night to stop theft. Poultry housing needs four things: space, ventilation, light and protection from weather and predators.

screens.title: Chickens indoors
screens.ask: Why do some families keep chickens inside the house at night?
screens.after: Keeping chickens inside at night protects them from thieves.

screens.title: 3.4.5 General management: 1. Housing
paras: Some households keep chickens inside the house at night, to stop theft.
Poultry housing has four basic needs.

screens.title: Key words
defs: Keeping fertile eggs warm until they hatch.

screens.text: Tap the four basic needs of poultry housing.
Poultry housing should protect birds from predators.
A chicken house is crowded, dark and has no windows. Which needs are missing?
screens.why: Crowded means no space, dark means no light, and no windows means no ventilation.
screens.clue: Check each of the four needs.

en.text: Incubation keeps fertile eggs warm until they hatch. In natural incubation, a large, healthy hen covers the eggs; give her feed and water nearby and keep humidity at 60–80 percent. Eggs become fertile about four days after a rooster joins the hens. In artificial incubation, an incubator uses electricity, gas or kerosene, with a thermostat keeping the temperature within one degree.

screens.title: Brainstorming
screens.ask: What does incubation of a chicken egg mean?
opts: Keeping the egg warm so a chick grows
screens.after: Incubation keeps fertile eggs warm until they hatch.

screens.title: A. Natural incubation
paras: Choose a large hen to cover and warm more eggs.
She should be healthy, vaccinated and a good mother.
Eggs become fertile about four days after a rooster joins the hens.
Keep feed and water near her, so eggs do not cool.
screens.note: In dry areas, damp soil under the nest keeps humidity at 60–80 percent.

screens.title: B. Artificial incubation
paras: Many incubators are sold, of different sizes.
Most use electricity; some use gas or kerosene.
A thermostat keeps the temperature constant within one degree Celsius.

screens.title: Key words
defs: A hen sits on the eggs and keeps them warm.
A machine (incubator) keeps eggs warm at a constant temperature.

screens.text: What is the difference between natural and artificial incubation?
opts: A hen warms the eggs vs. a machine warms the eggs
screens.ans: A hen warms the eggs vs. a machine warms the eggs
screens.why: Natural: a broody hen. Artificial: an incubator.
screens.clue: Who or what keeps the eggs warm?

screens.ask: In natural incubation, humidity should be between 60 and ___ percent.

screens.text: Feed and water should be placed far from the sitting hen.
screens.why: Near her, so she does not leave the eggs to cool.
screens.clue: Why should she stay on the nest?

screens.text: Yonas wants to hatch 200 eggs at once and has electricity. Which method fits?
screens.why: One hen can cover only a few eggs. An electric incubator holds many eggs at a constant temperature.
screens.clue: How many eggs can one hen cover?
